mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 declines over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production signals a strengthening economy, which increases corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 5% month-over-month and real GDP growth is negative, it signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 5% MoM and GDPC1 growth is negative
regime_hint: economic contraction with declining housing demand
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases > 5% MoM and GDPC1 growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and retail and food services sales are increasing, it signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which increases corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth is positive and RSAFS increases
regime_hint: economic expansion with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 growth is positive and RSAFS increases.
